name: Question 5
problem:
Write the following first-order linear ODE in standard form.

$$
y\frac{dy}{dx}+{x}^{2}y={y}^{2}x\,,\,y\ne 0\,.
$$
worked_solution:
A first-order linear ODE is in standard form if it is written as

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+P(x)y=Q(x)\,,
$$

Converting the given equation to standard form, we have

$$

$$

$$
\begin{aligned}y\frac{dy}{dx}+{x}^{2}y & ={y}^{2}x \\ y\frac{dy}{dx}+{x}^{2}y-{y}^{2}x & =0 \\ y(\frac{dy}{dx}+{x}^{2}-yx) & =0 \\ \frac{dy}{dx}+{x}^{2}-yx & =0 \\ \frac{dy}{dx}+\,{{(-x)}_{⏟}}_{P(x)}y & ={{-{x}^{2}}_{⏟}}_{Q(x)} \\ \frac{dy}{dx}-xy & =-{x}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the equation is written in standard form with $P(x)=-x$ and $Q(x)=-{x}^{2}.$

Question 5
?

Write the following first-order linear ODE in standard form. ydydx+x2y=y2x,y≠0.

a
dydx−xy=−x2
b
dydx+x2y=x
c
dydx−y=−2x
d
dydx=−x2
e
dydx+1−x21+x2y=1
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

A first-order linear ODE is in standard form if it is written as dydx+P(x)y=Q(x), Converting the given equation to standard form, we have ydydx+x2y=y2xydydx+x2y−y2x=0y(dydx+x2−yx)=0dydx+x2−yx=0dydx+(−x)⏟P(x)y=−x2⏟Q(x)dydx−xy=−x2

Now, the equation is written in standard form with P(x)=−x and Q(x)=−x2.
